messages.subject: variable correspondence between trajectories
messages.body_plain:
Hi - I recently found this package and am evaluating if I should use an upcoming DES project to learn it.  I will give a generic overview of the simulation I want to develop, please let me know if the nuances are possible in simmer.

Essentially, it is a simulation of the movement of three types of bags through a retail store - typeA, typeB, and typeC.  The trajectories for each bag type would be very similar:

arrival - appearance at a counter due to a purchase occurring
seizure of a store employee
bags spend X minutes being moved to a storage area specific for that bag type, each storage area with their own max capacity
release of a store employee
bags wait a specified Y minutes (storage area dwell time)
seizure of a store employee
retrieved from the storage area for Z minutes
release of a store employee
end

This seems very straightforward until I considered the inter-relatedness of these three trajectories.  For instance, a bag of typeA and a bag of typeB may arrive simultaneously from the same purchase, and I only need one store employee to move them to their storage areas (one bag each hand!).  However, these two bags may then be retreived from the storage area at the same time (requiring one seizure of a store employee), or at separate times, requiring two separate seizures of store employees (or two seizures of the same employee).

How might I go about including the following considerations in the trajectories:

1) Correlation between arrivals - I can identify an empirical probability that each purchase will contain one, two, or all three bag types.  How can I generate arrivals along trajectories that draw from a common empirical probability like this?

2) Correlation of the time spent in storage areas - sometimes, two bags from the same purchase will be removed from their respective storage areas simultaneously, sometimes not.  Can I write the storage area dwell time arguments for two bags, from the same purchase, so that sometimes the bags have the same dwell time, and sometimes they don't?

3) When moving multiple bags from the counter to the storage area, how do I only seize one employee even though they are on different bagtype-specific trajectories? Similarly, how do I seize an employee once if two bags of the same purchase are retrieved at the same time, but twice if they are retrieved at different times?

I know this is pretty specific, and I don't have any example code because I want to evaluate if simmer is appropriate before I start putting time into development in simmer vs. another DES software.

Thanks in advance.
Ralph Asher

Thanks Inaki.  So can I have a batch of 1-3 bag types arrive simultaneously, be carried as a batch to the storage area, then be "un-batched" and then seize storage areas individually?  Then be either re-batched or not, based upon when their timeout occurs, and then seize an employee either separately or not?

So for example, if a day has 1,120 purchases with the following distribution of bag batches:

Order Batches Bag Types Batch Count
TypeA 157
TypeB 197
TypeC 162
TypeATypeB 113
TypeATypeC 172
TypeBTypeC 120
TypeATypeBTypeC 199

The way I would understand it is, I have an arrival of a batch (a customer purchase) based upon some distribution, likely a nonstationary Poisson process.  I then assign the bagtype associated with the batch from this empirical distribution. Say the batch type is of TypeATypeC (i.e., one bag of each type).

The batch then seizes an employee and is moved to the storage areas, where it seizes one storage slot of Type A and one storage slot of Type C.  Then the timeout for Type A and Type C are not simultaneous.  Type A is stored for 30 minutes, Type C for 90 minutes.  Since the timeout is not simultaneous, then the bags seize an employee separately.  However, if the timeout for both Type A and Type C are 45 minutes, they can seize the same employee for retrieval.

As another wrinkle, I think that if I need to retrieve two bags simultaneously, then I can seize the same employee for two bags in the same storage area even if they are from different orders.  So can I batch bags based upon the purchase time, then batch them differently based upon the storage area and retrieval time?

Thanks
Ralph

> upon when their timeout occurs, and then seize an employee either separately

Bags should be always batched to seize an employee. A batch of 1 is
still a batch.

> So for example, if a day has 1,120 purchases with the following distribution
> of bag batches:
>
>
> Order Batches Bag Types Batch Count
> TypeA 157
> TypeB 197
> TypeC 162
> TypeATypeB 113
> TypeATypeC 172
> TypeBTypeC 120

> process.  I then assign the bagtype associated with the batch from this
> empirical distribution. Say the batch type is of TypeATypeC (i.e., one bag
> of each type).

The trajectory should be independent of the generation process, and
batches don't care about the type of the bags. The trajectory would be
something along the lines (matching your own description) of:

- batch of 3, with a negligible timeout
- seize an employee
- some delay
- release the employee
- separate the batch
- storage area dwell time
- ... and again, batch, seize, delay, release, separate

For the arrival process, if you use one generator, you should set an
attribute at the beginning of the trajectory to indicate the type of
bag, so that you can pick the correct dwell time.

You may also use 3 distinct generators, one per type, feeding 3
trajectories with different dwell times (I would take this approach).
Then, keep in mind that you must use a *named* batch (see the
documentation and specific examples in vignettes).

> The batch then seizes an employee and is moved to the storage areas, where
> it seizes one storage slot of Type A and one storage slot of Type C.  Then
> the timeout for Type A and Type C are not simultaneous.  Type A is stored
> for 30 minutes, Type C for 90 minutes.  Since the timeout is not
> simultaneous, then the bags seize an employee separately.  However, if the
> timeout for both Type A and Type C are 45 minutes, they can seize the same
> employee for retrieval.

> As another wrinkle, I think that if I need to retrieve two bags
> simultaneously, then I can seize the same employee for two bags in the same
> storage area even if they are from different orders.  So can I batch bags
> based upon the purchase time, then batch them differently based upon the
> storage area and retrieval time?

The sketch above solves all these nuances for you, because bags are
batched only if they concur during the batch timeout, regardless of
the bag type.

library(tidyverse)
library(simmer)

#sim clock is in minutes, so action times are in seconds divided by 60 seconds per minute
#front cashier inputs order
frontcashier_inputorder_action_time <- 180/60

backroomworker_floortravel_action_time <- 45/60
#backroomworker puts away order
backroomworker_inboundbackroom_action_time <- 120/60
#backroom worker retrieves order
backroomworker_outboundbackroom_action_time <- 60/60

AmbientBag_trajectory <- trajectory("Ambient Temp Bag Trajectory") %>%
  seize("frontcashier", 1) %>%
  #some variability around action time
  timeout(function() (frontcashier_inputorder_action_time * rnorm(n=1, mean=1, sd = 0.1)) %>%

  release("frontcashier", 1) %>%

  #now have backroom TM travel along floorspace... backroomworker is resource
  seize("backroomworker",1) %>%
  #some variability around action time

  timeout(function() (backroomworker_floortravel_action_time * rnorm(n=1, mean=1, sd = 0.1)) %>%
  release("backroomworker",1) %>%

  #now put the bag in the ambient storage area, use 1 space
  seize("ambient_storage_bag_space",1) %>%

  timeout(function() rpois(1, 300)) %>%
  #now the order is ready to be picked up
  seize("backroomworker", 1) %>%
  #some variability around action time
  timeout(function() (backroomworker_outboundbackroom_action_time * rnorm(n=1, mean=1, sd = 0.1))) %>%
  release("backroomworker",1)

  sim_env <- simmer("StoreSimulationEnvornment") %>%
    add_resource("frontcashier", 3) %>%
    add_resource("backroomworker", 2) %>%
    add_resource("ambient_storage_bag_space", 10) %>%
    add_generator("ambientbag", AmbientBag_trajectory, function() rpois(1,30)) %>%
    run(until=60*15)

messages.subject: New package: simmer.bricks
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

The new package simmer.bricks has found its way to CRAN. As discussed
in [1], there are high-level tasks or patterns that can be
conceptualised in concrete activity sequences without the need for
extending or changing the simmer API. This new package is intended to
capture this kind of patterns into usable *bricks*, i.e., methods that
can be used as activities, but return an arrangement of activities
implementing higher-level tasks.

Two good examples of this, already included in this initial release,
are "delayed_release" (discussed in this list and in [1]) and
"do_parallel" (discussed in [2]). Please, take a look at the
introductory vignette [3] for further discussion and examples.

The reference page [4] lists all the available methods. The examples
included in the help page for each method show the equivalence in
plain activities. This is very important if you want to mix bricks
with rollbacks to produce loops, as the rollback method works in
number of activities.

As always, we are more than happy to receive feedback and suggestions,
either via this list or via GitHub issues and PRs. If you identify any
pattern that you usually type over and over in your simulations and
you think it could become a useful simmer brick, please don't hesitate
to share it.

Regards,
Iñaki

[1] https://github.com/r-simmer/simmer/issues/124
[2] https://github.com/r-simmer/simmer/issues/132
[3] http://r-simmer.org/extensions/bricks/articles/introduction.html
[4] http://r-simmer.org/extensions/bricks/reference/index.html

I'm not familiar with repairable systems, but I would model each
subsystem's lifetime as a trajectory. For example, the lifetime of a
generic "part" would be something like the following (not tested):

part <- trajectory() %>%
  ## time to power on the system
  timeout(power_on) %>%
  ## subscribe to "system on/off" events
  trap("system on") %>%
  ## if an off is received, wait for repair and start again
  trap("system off",
       handler = trajectory() %>%
         wait() %>%
         ## back to timeout(power_on)
         rollback(4)) %>%
  ## the system is working
  timeout(working) %>%
  ## until this part fails and sends an off event
  untrap(c("system off", "system on")) %>%
  send("system off") %>%
  ## repairing
  seize("repair") %>%
  timeout(repairing) %>%
  release("repair") %>%
  ## signal on and back to timeout(power_on)
  send("system on") %>%
  rollback(10)

where "power_on" could be a constant, and "working" and "repairing"
are whatever stochastic processes you want.

Regards,
Iñaki

messages.body_plain:
OK, I'm reaching out for more help on how to batch.  In the code below, I have a separate trajectory for each bag type (ambient, refrigerated, and frozen - only ambient is shown for space purposes).  Interarrival times between bags of each time are exponentially distributed; generators create arrivals for each bag type in a Poisson process designed to have daily count of each bag type day proportional to a defined percentage of total.

So the next step is how to create orders!  I have an empirical CDF of number of bags in an order (batch).  Simplified,

60% of orders are one bag,
20% of orders are two bags,
10% of orders are three bags,
10% of orders are four bags.

So now I would appreciate some guidance on how to proceed from here.  I am thinking along these lines:

1) make batches with a randomly-selected size based upon the above empirical CDF (1,2,3,4 bags) and timeout=Inf.  I can assume that these 1, 2, 3, 4 bags are any permutation of ambient, refrigerated, and frozen bags, based upon the independent generators of the three bag types.
2) they move as a batch through the front cashier, being moved by the backroom worker to the storage areas
3) then they're unbatched and move to their respective storage areas.  Bag storage times can be assumed to be gamma-distributed.  If possible, I want to have the option that either:

3a) bag storage times within the same order are all identical - meaning they are placed in their respective temperature storage areas, but are retrieved simultaneously from a single sampling of the gamma distribution.  They then seize the same backroom worker and exit the system.
3b) bag storage times within the same order are unique, and are retrieved separtately from three samples of the gamma distribution.  They then seize the backroom worker separately and exit the system.
3c) for two bags from different initial batches, even if their expiration time in storage is nearly simultaneous, they need to seize separate backroom workers.

I'd appreciate any help on how to go forward from here.

Thanks
Ralph

====
library(tidyverse)
library(simmer)
library(simmer.plot)

#data input section:
#daily bags: assume exponential distibution / Poisson process
#and break down daily bag total based upon empirical observation of purchases
daily_bag_forecast <- 1000

pct_bags_ambient <- 0.4
pct_bags_refrig <- 0.3
pct_bags_frozen <- 0.3

#identify length of simulation clock based upon hours of store operation
hours_operation <- (21 - 9) #from 9am to 9pm
minutes_operation <- hours_operation * 60

#dwell time in bag storage is approximately gamma distributed
order_storage_gamma_shape = 3.6
order_storage_gamma_rate = 0.03

AmbientBag_trajectory <- trajectory("Ambient Temp Bag Trajectory") %>%

  set_attribute("trajectory_start_time", function() now(.env=store_sim_env))  %>%

  seize("frontcashier", 1) %>%
  #some variability around action time

  timeout(function() (120 * rnorm(n=1, mean=1, sd = 0.1))) %>%

  release("frontcashier", 1) %>%

  #now have backroom worker travel to cash register... backroomworker is resource

  seize("backroomworker",1) %>%
  #some variability around action time

  timeout(function() (120 * rnorm(n=1, mean=1, sd = 0.1))) %>%

  release("backroomworker",1) %>%

  set_attribute("storage_dwell_start_time", function() now(.env=store_sim_env))  %>%

  #now put the bag in the ambient storage area, use 1 space
  seize("ambient_storage_bag_space",1) %>%

  #use gamma distribution for backroom storage time based upon empirical evaluation of storage time
  timeout(function() rgamma(1, shape = order_storage_gamma_shape , rate = order_storage_gamma_rate)) %>%
  set_attribute("storage_dwell_end_time", function() now(.env=store_sim_env)) %>%
  set_attribute("storage_total_dwell_time", function() (get_attribute(.env=store_sim_env,keys="storage_dwell_end_time") - get_attribute(.env=store_sim_env,keys="storage_dwell_start_time"))) %>%
  release("ambient_storage_bag_space",1) %>%

  #now the order is ready to be picked up
  seize("backroomworker", 1) %>%
  #some variability around action time

  timeout(function() (45 * rnorm(n=1, mean=1, sd = 0.1))) %>%

  release("backroomworker",1) %>%

  set_attribute("carrier_pickup_time", function() now(.env=store_sim_env))

# snipped: similar trajectory RefrigBag_trajectory for refrigerated products, using refrigerated storage space
# snipped: similar trajectory FrozenBag_trajectory for frozen products, using refrigerated storage space

store_sim_env <- simmer("StoreSimulationEnvornment") %>%
  simmer::add_resource("frontcashier", 3) %>%
  simmer::add_resource("backroomworker",2) %>%
  simmer::add_resource("ambient_storage_bag_space",300) %>%
  simmer::add_resource("refrig_storage_bag_space", 300) %>%
  simmer::add_resource("frozen_storage_bag_space", 300) %>%
#generators for different bag types, poisson process with rate calculated by average number of bags expected to see in a day.
  simmer::add_generator("ambientbag", AmbientBag_trajectory, function() rpois(1,(minutes_operation/(daily_bag_forecast*pct_bags_ambient))),mon=2) %>%
  simmer::add_generator("refrigbag", RefrigBag_trajectory, function() rpois(1,(minutes_operation/(daily_bag_forecast*pct_bags_refrig))),mon=2) %>%
  simmer::add_generator("frozenbag", FrozenBag_trajectory, function() rpois(1,(minutes_operation/(daily_bag_forecast*pct_bags_frozen))),mon=2)

store_sim_env %>% run(minutes_operation)

distributor <- trajectory() %>%

    continue=rep(TRUE, 3),

    RefrigBag_trajectory,

Don't name the batch, so that they are exclusive for each trajectory.

>   set_attribute("trajectory_start_time", function() now(.env=store_sim_env))

You don't need to do this. simmer automatically monitors everything,

I think I've found a much cleaner way to go about this.  Prior to any of the simmer code, I have a function that returns a vector of ambient/refrigerated/frozen bags in each order.  This function uses empirical distributions of bag count per order, and temperature channels for each bag.

bag_tempchannel_samplefunction <- function(
  bag_count_vector = c(1,2,3,4),
  bag_prob_vector = c(.6, .2, 0.1, 0.1),
  bagtype_namevector = c('Ambient','Refrigerated','Frozen'),
  bagtype_bagpct_input = c(0.6,0.2,0.2)
)
{
#sample to make a number of bags in the order
  bagcount <- sample(x = bag_count_vector, size = 1, prob= bag_prob_vector)
#now sample from the bagtype_namevector to make the composition of the order
  vecout <- sample(x=bagtype_namevector,size=bagcount,replace=TRUE,prob=bagtype_bagpct_input)
  ambient_bagcount <- sum(vecout=='Ambient')
  refrig_bagcount <- sum(vecout=='Refrigerated')
  frozen_bagcount <- sum(vecout=='Frozen')

#now return a numeric vector equivalent to the character vector vecout

  return(c(ambient_bagcount,refrig_bagcount,frozen_bagcount))
}

I have a single trajectory for an "order". First thing in the trajectory, I set several attributes:

ambient bag count / refrigerated bag count / order bag count : from the bag_tempchannel_samplefunction. May be zero.
storage dwell time : same dwell time for the entire order, sampled from the gamma function

Then the trajectory for the order is almost the same as before:
seize front cashier for a time then release
seize backroom worker for a time then release

seize the individual storage areas, with the resource size being drawn from the bag count attributes:

  seize(resource="ambient_storage_bag_space", amount=function() get_attribute(.env=sim_env, keys= "ambient_bagcount")) %>%
  seize(resource="refrig_storage_bag_space",amount= function()get_attribute(.env=sim_env, keys= "refrig_bagcount")) %>%
  seize(resource="frozen_storage_bag_space", amount= function() get_attribute(.env=sim_env, keys= "frozen_bagcount")) %>%

hold for a time, then release using the same attributes.
seize backroom worker for a time then release
end of trajectory.

Looking at the system results this seems to be working properly, with correct-ish distributions of bag types and bag counts per order, and utilization of storage space.  Am I missing any big pieces that you can think of?

Ralph

Hi, I recently found this package.  I need to write some simulation code related with vessels loading inventory from a warehouse. One of the scenarios in the simulation is related with tides, which ones stop the operation and bringing some possible extra costs.

3) Vessel is loading cargo
4) Port is declared closed because tides and vessel did not complete cargo.
5) Port is opened
6) Vessel is loading the remaining cargo.
7) Vessel completed cargo
8) Vessel leaves port.

Is there some way to save the times between each ones of this activities for one vessel?

Sometimes the port is closed and the same vessel did not complete the cargo because the available operation time is not enough, is there some way to repeat the activity "loading cargo" until complete it?

This is my first experience writing this kind of codes, so I would be grateful if you can help me.

Matías

> Hi, I recently found this package.  I need to write some simulation code
> related with vessels loading inventory from a warehouse. One of the
> scenarios in the simulation is related with tides, which ones stop the
> operation and bringing some possible extra costs.

There are multiple ways of doing this. First of all, you need a model:
you need to decide what is a resource and what is a process; and
sometimes not, but sometimes it depends on the metrics you want to
compute.

> One possible scenario is:
>
> 1) Vessel arrives at port.
> 2) Port is opened.
> 3) Vessel is loading cargo
> 4) Port is declared closed because tides and vessel did not complete cargo.
> 5) Port is opened
> 6) Vessel is loading the remaining cargo.
> 7) Vessel completed cargo
> 8) Vessel leaves port.
>
> Is there some way to save the times between each ones of this activities for
> one vessel?

simmer provides automated monitoring of everything: each process'
lifetime is recorded; each time there's a change in a resource, it is
recorded. You have to think about your model, and automatically you'll
get data frames with everything that happened to compute summaries and
statistics.

> Sometimes the port is closed and the same vessel did not complete the cargo
> because the available operation time is not enough, is there some way to
> repeat the activity "loading cargo" until complete it?

If you model the port as a preemptive resource, then you can program
your tides to seize the whole port with maximum priority, so that
everything stops until the tide releases the port again. Then, vessels
automatically resume their activity.

> This is my first experience writing this kind of codes, so I would be
> grateful if you can help me.

There are numerous vignettes. I suggest you to start playing with the
code there, especifically those examples involving preemptive
resources.

>
> Matías

Hope this is enough explanation. Let me know if you need a small example. Help would be hugely appreciated!

Kind regards,

Andre

messages.subject: Re: Model Validation and testing
messages.body_plain:
Verification and validation of simulation models (especially Discrete Event models) is a topic that has been studied in depth for a very long time.
There is almost always a tutorial given each year at the Winter Simulation Conference, for which proceedings are publicly available.
https://informs-sim.org/

Also, an introduction to the topic can be found in most any undergraduate discrete event simulation textbook.
